done_when: Close judges the pull request checks only on the head it pushed and never counts a result from an earlier head (it says it is waiting instead), and a failed push is retried a few times with backoff before close gives up.

findings.body: This test sets FORGE_PUSH_WAIT to 0.5, so it never checks the delay used by a normal `forge close`. If the default in `src/forge/close.py:238` changed to zero, this test would still pass, and test 2 checks only the number of attempts. Add a Close run without the override that verifies increasing delays.
findings.title: Not done: the default push backoff test

findings.body: The new environment variable exists to shorten the timing test, as the adjacent comment states. Close needs a fixed backoff, and testing its normal 1, 2 and 4 second waits through the command would remove this extra runtime setting.
findings.title: Simpler: remove FORGE_PUSH_WAIT → test the fixed retry schedule

why: Close pushes its review commit while the pull request check still shows the previous head's result, so close reports failed checks and every close needs a second run; a push that fails once with a passing git error also stops close
